LESSON: COHERENCE WRITING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Writing 3.1 Guided Writing (Vocabulary) (1 session) By the end of the sub- stran
Topic 3.9: Coherence Writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Coherence Writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we ensure our writing is coherent?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify coherence markers in writing
2. write coherent texts using guided writing strategies

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COHERENCE WRITING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Coherence Writing helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: COHERENCE WRITING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify coherence markers in writing

What this means
In this part you learn to identify coherence markers in writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify coherence markers in writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Coherence Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify coherence markers in writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write coherent texts using guided writing strategies

What this means
In this part you learn to write coherent texts using guided writing strategies. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write coherent texts using guided writing strategies.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Coherence Writing to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write coherent texts using guided writing strategies. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Coherence Writing is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Coherence Writing”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify coherence markers in writing)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Coherence Writing to a partner. (skill: write coherent texts using guided writing strategies)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Coherence Writing to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify coherence markers in writing.
3. Practise this skill: write coherent texts using guided writing strategies.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Coherence Writing from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Coherence Writing: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Coherence Writing?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we ensure our writing is coherent?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Coherence Writing means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify coherence markers in writing.
5. Be able to: write coherent texts using guided writing strategies.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
